data.title: Structured Output
data.tagline: Model output returned in an agreed, machine-checkable shape
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish structured output, JSON, and business validation.
data.description: To fill a calendar form from an email, a product can require fields such as title, date, and location with defined types. JSON is a common encoding, not the same thing as structured output, and business rules still need validation.

learning.assumes: You have used a form, calendar, or feature that fills in information automatically.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish structured output, JSON, and business validation.

explanation.title: Define the shape
explanation.text: Specify fields such as title, date, and location before asking the model to extract them.

explanation.title: Return the agreed fields
explanation.text: The model returns data in the required structure rather than a free-form summary.

explanation.title: Validate before use
explanation.text: The product checks the schema and real business rules before filling a form or creating an event.

data.boundary: Valid JSON and a matching schema do not prove that a date or location is real or usable.

lessonPractice.title: A page must render model results as task cards. Which return format is most reliable?

options.label: Request structured output matching a task-field schema and validate required fields
options.feedback: Correct. Stable fields let software render, validate, and handle omissions reliably.

options.label: Ask for prose and guess title and due date with string rules
options.feedback: Natural-language formats change, making parsing brittle and omissions hard to detect.

options.label: Ask the model to return full task-card HTML
options.feedback: Model-generated display HTML is hard to validate safely; return data and let the UI render it.

data.agentPrompt: Make task extraction return a fixed shape: title is required text; dueDate is YYYY-MM-DD or null; owner is text or null; status is one of todo, doing, done. Reject a missing title, invalid date, or unknown status before use; keep an absent due date as null rather than guessing. Test complete, no-date, and invalid-status inputs.
